facts: Geoffrey R. Grimmett authored the paper 'SAWs, trails, kites, patterns' posted to arXiv on October 31, 2026.

On a vertex-transitive graph G, the number of n-step self-avoiding walks (SAWs) has order μ(G)^n, and the number of n-step trails has order μ_T(G)^n, where μ(G) is the connective constant and μ_T(G) is the trail constant.
The connective constant μ and the trail constant μ_T are immediately equal (μ = μ_T) if G has degree 3 or less, or if G is a tree.
The paper establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for the strict inequality μ < μ_T when G has degree 4 or more, is not a tree, and possesses a height function.
The condition for μ < μ_T is satisfied whenever the height function of G is transitive.
The core proof relies on a pattern theorem for graphs possessing height functions, utilizing an unpublished argument for Z^d by Hammersley reported by Janse van Rensburg et al. (1996).
The paper includes ancillary results concerning self-avoiding walks on the line graph of G.
